scope: 70 exact original source performances, including 64 Hebrew verse clips from the distinct 2018 Rosh Hashanah document. No independent singing synthesis or reviewed word timing inferred.

studies.name: Tiberian pronunciation · Genesis 1:1–13
studies.sourceTitle: Geoffrey Khan, The Tiberian Pronunciation Tradition of Biblical Hebrew, Volume I (2020), §I.5.4.1, pp. 614–618
studies.coverageStatus: Publication identifies passage. No source-edition comparison or word/syllable/audio alignment is supplied by this app. Opening the text displays unchanged UXLC.
studies.description: A scholarly reconstruction of Tiberian pronunciation, performed by Alex Foreman in two dagesh readings and with or without a source-labeled Sefardi melody. These are fixed performances, with their original pronunciation, pitch and timing.
studies.limits: This study is separate from the six historical Kinnor Accent labels and from a complete communal melody grammar. The recordings do not provide independently controllable singing synthesis.

rightsEvidence.location: Volume I copyright page; recorded material credited to Alex Foreman, CC BY; book CC BY 4.0.
rightsEvidence.resourceListLocation: §I.5.4.1, printed p. 614; four Genesis 1:1–13 audio DOIs.
rightsEvidence.retrieval: Official pages/PDF text read through web tool. Direct PDF download returned405; publisher page direct curl returned429. No PDF bytes or visual transcription claimed.

studies.coverageStatus: A recorded cantillation-name table. No Torah-passage, word, syllable or note mapping is inferred.

studies.description: Dr. Isabel Bard’s 2021 recording of Torah cantillation names, identified by its primary archive as Western Ashkenazi. The unchanged original retains the performer’s voice, pitch and timing.

studies.name: Rosh Hashanah · 2018 source verse recordings
studies.sourceTitle: Len Fellman, Rosh Hashanah Torah readings (2018 source document)
studies.coverageStatus: Source verse identified by original embedded filename. The reader opens unchanged UXLC; source-edition comparison and word boundaries remain unreviewed.

pronunciations.name: As recorded · pronunciation not separately identified

studies.description: 64 original Hebrew verse recordings: Genesis 21:1–34, Genesis 22:1–24 and Numbers 29:1–6, extracted unchanged from the 2018 Rosh Hashanah document. The document is by Len Fellman; its embedded-audio performer is not separately credited.
studies.limits: Fixed source recordings retain original pronunciation, melody, pitch and timing. They are not independently pronounced singing presets, a complete melody grammar or Kinnor realizations. The document credits Joshua R. Jacobson’s book for melodies; no modern score or inferred named tradition is imported.
